fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. The LORD says, "…I will make a way in the wilderness and streams in the desert." (Isaiah 43:19). He says it right after "I am about to do something new." A wilderness doesn't usually come with a road, so a way there is something new.

True, friend. The LORD says, "The people I formed for Myself will declare My praise." (Isaiah 43:21). Notice He says "will," not "might" and not "maybe." He formed them for Himself, and praise is what He says they will declare.

That's it. The LORD says, "But you have not called on Me, O Jacob, because you have grown weary of Me, O Israel." (Isaiah 43:22). I'll say it plainly, this part is heavy. They have not called on Him, and He says they have grown weary of Him.
Right. The LORD says He blots out their transgressions and "…remembers your sins no more." (Isaiah 43:25). He says He does it for His own sake. That's a promise worth reading twice.

Yes, friend. The LORD says, "Remind Me, let us argue the matter together. State your case, so that you may be vindicated." (Isaiah 43:26). He opens the floor, and that's quite an invitation. He even says the goal is that they may be vindicated.

True, friend. The LORD says, "Your first father sinned, and your spokesmen rebelled against Me." (Isaiah 43:27). The text doesn't name the first father there, so I'll leave it right where the text does. The same verse adds that their spokesmen rebelled against Him.

Close, but the verse isn't naming Isaiah. The LORD says, "For your sake, I will send to Babylon…" (Isaiah 43:14), and "your" means the people He's speaking to. Whoever carries the message, it's for them.

I get why it sounds right, since conquerors and ships feel like they go together. But the verse goes the other direction. The LORD brings them "as fugitives" (Isaiah 43:14), people on the run, not people riding in on top.
The Jordan is a famous name, but it isn't mentioned here. The LORD says, "…I will make a way in the wilderness and streams in the desert." (Isaiah 43:19). The way goes through the wilderness.

That's right. The LORD provides water in the wilderness and rivers in the desert "…to give drink to My chosen people." (Isaiah 43:20). The water has an address, and it's them. The jackals and ostriches honor Him because of it too (Isaiah 43:20).

The Chaldeans were just in the story, so I see how they stuck around. But the verse names who gets the drink: "…to give drink to My chosen people." (Isaiah 43:20). Back in verse 14, the Chaldeans are the ones brought as fugitives.

Good guess, since armies show up in verse 17. But the LORD isn't talking about fighting here. He says, "But you have not called on Me, O Jacob…" (Isaiah 43:22). He's talking about them calling on Him.

Sending them back is a fair guess, but it isn't what He says. The LORD says, "I, yes I, am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake and remembers your sins no more." (Isaiah 43:25). He blots them out Himself.
